correctness.rationale: The published H-description gives every facet normal and support value. After intrinsic projection to the sum hyperplane, the singleton facets have the displayed radius. For a general support of size t, the projected-normal quantity H satisfies H<=sqrt(Q), while the positive coefficient vector gives W-H>=t-sqrt(t). The published kappa formula is bounded by \(3^{t+1}/2+1\); these inequalities prove strict separation for all large supports and all but five small ambient/support pairs. Those five pairs reduce to exact rational squared-distance comparisons with strictly positive certified minima. Finally, summing the singleton ball constraints gives the matching global upper bound and forces the uniform center uniquely.

value.rationale: The simple permutoassociahedron is a canonical simple polytope designed to combine permutohedral and associahedral structures and to model associativity/commutativity coherence. Its explicit realization contains exponentially scaled families of nonparallel truncation facets, so it is not a priori clear that the original singleton-simplex inball survives all cuts. The theorem gives an exact all-dimensional metric invariant, identifies the unique center, and completely classifies the contact facets.
